podcast.body: The remix of Taylor Swift's 2015 hit "Bad Blood" featured "an actual rapper," Kendrick Lamar, brought in to enhance its "hip-hop swagger." This collaboration underscored the song's impact and the crossover appeal of diss tracks, even outside traditional rap. "It thumped with hip-hop swagger and so for the remix, Swift brought in as a guest an actual rapper. His name Kendrick Lamar."

podcast.body: This 2015 smash hit from Taylor Swift was "about a feud Swift had with fellow pop star Katy Perry about some backup dancers Perry allegedly stole from Swift's tour." Its hip-hop swagger was further enhanced by a remix featuring Kendrick Lamar, which helped it become a major pop and chart success. "Swift called the song appropriately enough, bad blood."

podcast.body: This song became a number one hit during Taylor Swift's first fully imperial phase, which peaked in 2014 and 2015, demonstrating her strong chart performance even with what might be considered "second tier singles." "This was her first fully Imperial phase, when even second tier singles like Bad Blood were hitting number one."
